cards.headline: 603 launch auctions.
cards.subline: Read directly off Robinhood Chain. No indexer in between.
cards.post:
GAVEL is a verdict layer for launch auctions on Robinhood Chain.

603 auctions have run through Uniswap's liquidity launcher. 133 became pools.

We read every one of them off the chain directly and publish what the parameters actually say.

No wallet connect. Nothing to approve.

cards.headline: The chain emits no event
cards.subline: A failed auction and an abandoned one look identical from the logs.
cards.post:
Something we did not expect.

When a launch auction draws no bids, the chain says nothing. No event. It just sits past its migration block in silence.

Which looks identical to an auction that cleared and was never migrated.

Two outcomes, one shape in the logs.

cards.headline: 433 auctions never cleared.
cards.subline: Nobody bid enough for there to be anything to migrate.
cards.post:
We assumed the gap between 603 auctions and 133 pools was abandonment.

It is not.

Asking each auction contract directly: 433 never reached a clearing price. Every auction that did clear was migrated. Not one was left sitting.

Most launches simply draw no bids.

cards.headline: No wallet connect.
cards.subline: GAVEL reads the chain. It never asks you for a signature.
cards.post:
GAVEL will never ask you to connect a wallet.

There is no approve step, no signature, no contract of ours you interact with. It reads public chain state and publishes what it finds.

A tool that tells you what is safe should not itself be something you have to trust with funds.

cards.headline: A model can lower a verdict.
cards.subline: The ceiling is arithmetic. Judgment only sits underneath it.
cards.post:
How GAVEL stops a language model talking a bad launch up.

Deterministic checks compute a ceiling from chain state alone. The model reasons on top and may lower the verdict below it.

It cannot raise it. A launch that fails a hard check can never be argued into a PASS.

cards.headline: Don't trust the verdict.
cards.subline: Every check is deterministic. Every input is a public call.
cards.post:
Every verdict page lists the exact transaction, auction contract, token and recipient it was derived from.

Not so the page looks thorough. So you can run the same calls and get the same answer without us.

A number that cannot be reproduced from chain state should not be here.

cards.headline: PASS does not mean safe.
cards.subline: We can read the launch parameters. We cannot read intent.
cards.post:
Worth saying plainly, because the opposite reading is how people lose money.

PASS means the deterministic checks found nothing structurally wrong with how the launch was configured.

It is not a price prediction, and not a claim the token is a good idea.

cards.headline: 21 auctions are open
cards.subline: The only page where a reader can still act on what it says.
cards.post:
Every other page on GAVEL is a record of something already decided.

/live is the one that matters while it still matters: auctions that have not passed their migration block, read straight from the chain in your browser.

The only page where you can still act on it.

cards.headline: $GAVEL is live on Virtuals.
cards.subline: The token buys API passes. It can never touch a verdict.
